Dataset scope, attribution & learning references

Human Reference Atlas female reference — 956 modelled parts. Original anatomical assets by Kristen Browne and Heidi Schlehlein, distributed under CC BY 4.0. See the HRA 3D Reference Library and NIH female body reference.

Uses HRA female v1.10 geometry with the female v1.5 pelvic bone supplement, from optimised files in Human Atlas. This lesson retains 956 adult female source meshes and excludes borrowed male bones, a separate donor’s leg muscles and pregnancy structures. Adaptations include mesh optimisation, binary repacking, display colours, filters and teaching controls. Full attribution.

This is a whole-body female reference with uneven coverage, not a complete inventory of female anatomy. Bone and muscle coverage is partial; detailed mapped brain regions account for many selectable parts. Modelled parts do not equal a standard count of organs. The female lesson is not the male BodyParts3D dataset, and its geometry is not registered to the separate heart model. Separation moves parts for study and does not depict anatomical positions.

Introductory learning text checked against the National Cancer Institute’s female reproductive anatomy overview. Source structure names remain English; Hausa group summaries await educator review. Educational study aid, not a clinical or surgical guide. Three.js and fflate use MIT licences.
